subject: Provisional subprocessor: Pulselytics temporary analytics bridge - action requested
messages:
From: Igor Sokolov <igor@dataflow.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Provisional subprocessor: Pulselytics temporary analytics bridge

Hi Vivek,

Looping you in from ClearPrice — we're evaluating Redwood for a pilot and had a last-minute ask from infra: they want to route anonymized telemetry through a short-lived analytics bridge provider (Pulselytics) during the trial window to avoid adding load to their existing stack. Pulselytics would only process inferential telemetry (no customer prompt text), store only derived metrics, and retain logs for a maximum of 72 hours before auto-deletion.

Key points from Pulselytics that matter to us:
- Processing location: EU-only by default; US fallback in case of capacity issues (they claim toggled region controls).
- Data types: metrics, event aggregates, sampling-level hashes (no PII or raw prompt contents).
- Security: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest; they propose using a customer-managed KMS key (customer can bring key).
- Timeline: provisional onboarding for the 30-day pilot starting next week, after which ClearPrice will re-evaluate.

I've attached a short scope doc (analytics-bridge-scope.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's stance on provisional subprocessors for trials and whether this needs a DPA amendment / customer notice? ClearPrice asked we notify you ASAP.

Thanks,
Igor
DataFlow (platform team)

Attachment: analytics-bridge-scope.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Igor Sokolov <igor@dataflow.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional subprocessor: Pulselytics temporary analytics bridge

Thanks Igor — appreciate the heads up and the clear summary. A few immediate clarifications we need before we can sign off to ClearPrice: 

1) Confirm the exact data fields Pulselytics will receive (sample schema).
2) Proof of on-demand region restriction (EU-only enforcement + failover behavior).
3) SOC2 / ISO27001 snapshot or attestation and whether they allow a scoped security questionnaire.
4) Confirm KMS integration details and whether customer-managed keys are actually supported in the short window.

Kimberly — can you weigh in on whether we treat this as a temporary subprocessor (notice only) or if it requires a DPA addendum for pilot-level access? Mina / Neha — please flag any operational risks (logging, KV cache exposure, or telemetry content that could include derived prompt hashes).

If we can get the items above by EOD tomorrow we should be able to provide a formal yes/no for the pilot.

Cheers,
Vivek
Senior Product Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen@pulselytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Igor Sokolov <igor@dataflow.io>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional subprocessor: Pulselytics temporary analytics bridge

Hi Vivek — quick follow-up from Pulselytics. Attaching the requested dataflow diagram (dataflow-diagram.png) and a link to our EU residency page. Answers inline: 

- Fields: we receive event_type, timestamp, anonymized_request_id (64-bit hash), latency_ms, model_version, sampling_flag. No prompt text.
- Region controls: you can pin processing to eu-west-1 via our control plane; fallback to us-east-1 only triggers if eu capacity is exhausted and only after explicit gated alerting to the partner.
- Controls: SOC2 Type II report available (we can provide recent page scan or NDA'd access).
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS; for short pilots we can accept ephemeral keys but recommend a managed key for auditing.

Link: https://pulselytics.com/residency-eu (public page)

Happy to run through the attestation live if that helps.

Best,
Ellen Park
Pulselytics — Integrations

Attachment: dataflow-diagram.png (image, 220KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Harlan Jacobs <harlan.jacobs@keenlegal.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T13:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional subprocessor: Pulselytics temporary analytics bridge

Team — thanks for the details. Quick legal / compliance read: 

- Classification: this is a subprocessor relationship. For a pilot we normally proceed with a notice + scoped questionnaire and an attestation rather than a full DPA amendment, provided processing is limited and no customer content (prompts) is exposed.
- Required items before notice: SOC2 evidence (scan or report), confirmation of EU-only pinning for the pilot, and a written retention guarantee (72 hours) with automated deletion proof. If Pulselytics cannot provide automated deletion logs, we require ClearPrice to sign a contingency clause limiting trial duration.
- Export control: unclear whether hashing and derived metrics are considered controlled for ClearPrice (they're EU-headquartered with some regulated clients). Ask Pulselytics to confirm they do not transfer derived aggregates outside EU for regulated tenant IDs.

Harlan (external counsel) — please advise if the retention guarantee + pinned region + KMS bring-your-own-key is sufficient for a notice-only path or if we should prepare a short DPA addendum template.

Action items: Vivek to get explicit written confirmation from Pulselytics on the three items above; Mina/Neha to draft temporary routing policy notes so infra can toggle the bridge on/off with safe defaults.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Head of Trust & Legal, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@pulselytics.com>, Igor Sokolov <igor@dataflow.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional subprocessor: Pulselytics temporary analytics bridge - action requested

Ellen / Igor — thanks for the fast turnaround and the diagram. Quick summary / decision for ClearPrice's pilot: 

1) Conditional approval for EU-pinned pilot only (no automatic US failover unless explicitly consented by ClearPrice).
2) Pulselytics must provide SOC2 evidence (redacted report or an attestation) and confirm automatic deletion logs are available within 7 days of deletion.
3) KMS: they must support customer-managed keys for the pilot; if not possible, we require a scoped logging exception and additional monitoring.

If Pulselytics can confirm (in writing) items 2 and 3 and update their residency page to note the EU pinning guarantee for ClearPrice, we will proceed with a notice-only subprocessor path (no DPA amendment for this 30-day trial). Otherwise we will pause and request a short DPA addendum.

Next steps: Pulselytics to reply with the confirmations and attach the SOC2 evidence. Mina / Neha: I'll sync with infra to hold the bridge toggle until paperwork is in place.

Vivek
Senior Product Lead, Redwood Inference
